name: Express
desc: Minimal unopinionated Node HTTP framework. Use when you want no magic and every tutorial on the internet to apply.

name: Fastify
desc: Fast Node framework with schema-based validation built in. Use when throughput and typed routes both matter.

name: NestJS
desc: Angular-style modules and DI for Node. Use on large teams that want enforced structure.

name: Hono
desc: Tiny web framework that runs on every JS runtime and edge platform. Use for edge functions and small APIs.

name: Django
desc: Batteries-included Python framework with ORM, admin and auth. Use when you want a working back office on day one.

name: FastAPI
desc: Async Python APIs with automatic OpenAPI docs from type hints. Use for ML services and modern Python APIs.

name: Flask
desc: Micro Python framework you assemble yourself. Use for small services and internal scripts with a web face.

name: Laravel
desc: Full-stack PHP with ORM, queues, auth and scheduling. Use when one developer must cover the whole product.

name: Ruby on Rails
desc: Convention over configuration, generators for everything. Use to go from idea to CRUD app in a day.

name: Spring Boot
desc: The enterprise Java standard: DI, data, security, actuators. Use where compliance and long support windows rule.

name: Gin
desc: Fast minimal Go HTTP router. Use for high-throughput services where you want explicit control.

name: ASP.NET Core
desc: High-performance cross-platform .NET web framework. Use in Microsoft shops and for latency-sensitive managed services.

name: Phoenix
desc: Elixir framework with LiveView and channels. Use for real-time dashboards and chat without writing a SPA.

name: GraphQL
desc: One typed endpoint where clients ask for exactly the fields they need. Use when many different clients hit one backend.

name: tRPC
desc: End-to-end typed procedure calls with no schema or codegen. Use in a TypeScript monorepo where client and server ship together.

name: OpenAPI / Swagger
desc: Describes a REST API so docs, clients and mocks can be generated. Use when external teams consume your API.

name: gRPC
desc: Binary RPC over HTTP/2 with generated clients. Use for chatty internal service-to-service traffic.

name: Firebase
desc: Google BaaS: Firestore, auth, storage, functions and hosting. Use for realtime mobile apps where documents beat tables.

name: Supabase
desc: Postgres with auth, storage, realtime and an auto-generated API the browser calls directly, guarded by row-level security. Use when you want a BaaS but refuse to give up SQL. It is the backend: no separate server needed.

name: Appwrite
desc: Open-source BaaS you can run yourself. Use when you want Firebase ergonomics inside your own infrastructure.

name: PocketBase
desc: One Go binary with SQLite, auth, files and an admin UI. Use for small self-hosted apps and prototypes.

name: Convex
desc: Reactive TypeScript backend where queries update the UI automatically. Use for collaborative apps with live state.

name: Supabase Edge Functions
desc: TypeScript functions on Deno, deployed beside your Supabase project with its keys and database already wired in. Use for webhooks, payment callbacks and any call that holds a secret the browser must not see.

name: Cloudflare Workers
desc: V8 isolates in hundreds of cities with no cold start, plus Cron Triggers, KV and Durable Objects. Use for APIs and middleware that must answer close to the user.

name: AWS Lambda
desc: Pay-per-invocation functions triggered by nearly every AWS event source. Use when uploads, queue messages or HTTP calls should run code with no server to keep alive.

name: Deno Deploy
desc: Globally distributed Deno isolates with built-in KV, queues and cron, deployed from git. Use for TypeScript APIs you want live with no build step and no infrastructure.

name: BullMQ
desc: Redis-backed job queue and repeatable schedules for Node, with retries and rate limits. Use when you already run a long-lived Node worker. On Supabase or serverless, use Inngest, Trigger.dev or QStash instead.

name: Celery
desc: Distributed task queue for Python, with Celery Beat for periodic tasks. Use when Django or FastAPI work must move off the request thread.

name: Sidekiq
desc: Threaded Redis-backed jobs for Rails. Use as the default background processor in any Rails app.

name: Inngest
desc: Durable event-driven functions with steps, retries and cron, no queue to run. It calls your functions over HTTP, so it needs an endpoint: a Next.js route, a Supabase Edge Function or any API. Use on serverless where you cannot keep a worker alive.

name: Socket.IO
desc: WebSocket abstraction with rooms, fallbacks and reconnection. Use for chat and live cursors on your own server.

name: Pusher
desc: Hosted pub/sub channels over WebSockets. Use when you want realtime without operating socket servers.

name: Ably
desc: Realtime messaging with guaranteed ordering and delivery. Use when dropped events would be a correctness bug.

name: Liveblocks
desc: Presence, comments and conflict-free collaborative state. Use to add multiplayer to an editor or canvas.
